meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 0.38% to 25,387.40 and Nifty Bank rose 1.13% to 62,273.25 after a record intraday high; foreign investors bought ₹4,195 crore (provisional); the rupee rose 43 paise to 93.51.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Wed 18 Nov: NIFTY 50 ends 0.38% higher at 25,387.40; Nifty Bank rises 1.13%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 0.38% to 25,387.40 and the Sensex 0.52% to 82,532.19 on Tuesday, a second day of gains led by bank shares; Nifty Bank rose 1.13% to 62,273.25 after touching a record intraday high of 62,379.15 (Upstox News, Liquide).
The NIFTY Midcap 100 rose 0.25% and the Smallcap 100 fell 0.22%, while Nifty IT fell 0.90% (Kotak Neo).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹4,195 crore and domestic institutions ₹197 crore (provisional, Kotak Neo, CNBC-TV18). The rupee rose 43 paise to 93.51 per dollar, its strongest close in seven months (PTI).
Overseas, the Dow fell 1.64%, the S&P 500 1.03% and the Nasdaq 0.74% ahead of Nvidia's results, which were released after the close (AP).
IBJA's morning rates on Tuesday put gold at ₹1,34,418 per 10 g and silver at ₹1,68,950 per kg (IBJA).

outlook.headline: Inflation above the RBI's band, softer bond yields and 12 sessions of foreign buying frame the week

drivers.title: Inflation and the RBI
drivers.text: October retail inflation rose to 6.09% from 5.54%, above the RBI's 6% upper limit for the first time in two years, with food inflation at 8.94%. ICRA's Aditi Nayar called a further 25 basis point rise in December nearly certain, and DBS Bank and 360 ONE Asset also expect a rise at the 2 to 4 December meeting (Outlook Business). Rate expectations reach bond yields, deposit rates and loan rates.

drivers.title: Bond yields and crude
drivers.text: India's 10-year government bond yield fell about 7 basis points to 7.27% on Tuesday as crude was lower during Indian trading, easing worries about imported inflation (Trading Economics). Brent later settled 0.76% higher at $93.14; the IEA expects supply to exceed demand by about 2 million barrels a day this quarter (Transport Topics). Oil reaches India through the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Foreign flows and the rupee
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹88,363 crore of Indian shares from 1 to 17 November (provisional, Kotak Neo), and CNBC-TV18 said their buying has run for 12 sessions. PTI said the inflows and softer crude helped the rupee rise 43 paise to 93.51. Flows reach large-cap demand and the currency.

global_cues.title: US shares and Nvidia
global_cues.text: On Tuesday the Dow fell 1.64%, the S&P 500 1.03% and the Nasdaq 0.74%, with software shares broadly lower, before Nvidia's results (Reuters, AP). Global technology sentiment reaches Indian IT shares and foreign investors' allocation between markets.

global_cues.title: US yields, the dollar and the Fed
global_cues.text: The US 10-year yield ended near 5.10%, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a December Fed rate rise at 95.4% (AP, Reuters). US yields and the dollar reach India through the rupee and foreign flows into emerging markets.

global_cues.title: Europe and Asia
global_cues.text: The FTSE 100 fell 1.76%, its worst day in eight months, and European shares broadly fell on AI-related worries (Reuters). In Asia the Kospi fell 2.6% and the Nikkei 1.34% on Tuesday (AP, Reuters). Regional moves shape the mood at India's open.

events.text: Official data are due. Estimates include SBI Ecowrap about 7.8%, Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis 7.4% and the RBI 7.2% (Business Today).

events.title: RBI policy meeting
events.text: ICRA and 360 ONE Asset expect a 25 basis point rise from a repo rate of 5.50%, and DBS Bank expects a second successive rise (Outlook Business).

global.headline: US shares fell for a second day as AI-linked stocks declined before Nvidia's results
global.note: Closes are for Tuesday 17 Nov. Germany's DAX fell more than 2% (Reuters); other European closes are not shown because only one published source gave the level.

us.title: The session
us.text: The Dow lost 1.64%, the S&P 500 1.03% and the Nasdaq 0.74% as investors cut holdings of AI-linked shares ahead of Nvidia's results; about 17 of every 20 S&P 500 stocks fell (AP).

us.title: Software and banks
us.text: Software names led the losses, with Salesforce, Workday, Intuit and Adobe down 4.3% to 9.5%; JPMorgan fell 2.4%, and Home Depot also fell 2.4% (Reuters, AP).

us.title: Nvidia after the bell
us.text: Nvidia closed 0.4% lower, then reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, with data centre revenue of $107.6 billion; it guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter, plus or minus 3% (Nvidia filing). Its shares rose as much as 3% in extended trading (Reuters).

events.title: Markets price a December Fed rise
events.text: Fed funds futures implied a 95.4% chance of a 25 basis point rise in December (CME FedWatch, reported by Reuters). The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: New US curbs on chip access for China
events.text: Washington moved to further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from firms such as Nvidia, ahead of a planned meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi (Reuters). The channel to India: risk appetite for Asian technology shares and regional fund flows.

events.title: A reported drone strike in Bahrain and an oil surplus outlook
events.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said drones hit a US radar site in Bahrain, while the IEA projects an oil surplus this quarter (Financial News). The channel to India: crude prices, the import bill and the rupee.

events.title: Bank of England rise priced
events.text: After UK wage growth slowed to 3.6% and unemployment dipped to 4.6%, traders saw about a 90% chance of a December Bank of England rise (Reuters). The channel to India: global rates and the dollar.

commentary.text: Gold stayed near its lowest level in more than a year as traders priced a December Fed rise; CME FedWatch put the chance at 95.7% during Asian trading, and the dollar touched a 19-month high (Reuters).
Kyle Rodda of Capital.com said gold is trading on expectations for Fed policy next year and on how high US rates can go (Reuters).

Later in the US session the dollar eased and Treasury yields fell, which steadied gold, while silver gained about 1% (Kitco). ANZ analysts said silver tends to move more sharply than gold and has weaker demand of its own (Reuters).

stories.headline: SEBI is weighing limits on new margin-funded share purchases, Reuters reported
stories.what: Citing two unnamed sources, Reuters reported that SEBI is considering stopping fresh margin trading facility positions in a stock once margin-funded holdings reach about 5% to 10% of its free float; the limits are not final. The margin trading book stands at ₹1.53 lakh crore, up 29% in a year, with about two-thirds in small and mid caps (Business Today, Kotak Neo). No rule has changed.
stories.why: Margin funding is borrowed money used to buy shares, so any limit would reach leveraged demand for heavily margin-funded small and mid caps.

stories.headline: The government raised export levies on diesel to ₹14 a litre and on jet fuel to ₹12.50 a litre
stories.what: In its fortnightly review, the Finance Ministry raised the diesel export levy from ₹11.50 to ₹14 a litre and the jet fuel (ATF) export duty from ₹11 to ₹12.50 a litre from 16 Nov; the petrol export levy stays at zero. It is the second rise in three weeks (Daily Jagran, IANS).
stories.why: The levies set how much refiners keep on fuel exports, so they reach the margins of export-oriented refiners.

stats.detail: End-October, from ₹82.64 lakh crore at end-September; AMFI cited a market uptick and positive net inflows

highlights.text: Among hybrid funds, arbitrage funds took a net ₹3,929 crore after a ₹3,956 crore outflow in September, which AMFI says drove the rise in hybrid fund net inflows; balanced advantage and dynamic asset allocation funds had a net outflow of ₹853 crore.
Silver ETFs took a net ₹3,092 crore, up from ₹1,974 crore in September, and gold ETFs ₹3,474 crore, down from ₹4,451 crore.

Large and mid cap funds took ₹8,484 crore against ₹4,271 crore in September, while small cap inflows fell to ₹6,407 crore from ₹9,039 crore and mid cap to ₹4,893 crore from ₹7,835 crore. Total folios rose to 28.78 crore from 28.62 crore.

fund_news.text: SEBI data show eight entities awaiting in-principle approval for a mutual fund licence, including IIFL Capital Services, Nirmal Bang Securities, Jainam Broking and Godrej Wealth and Asset Management; two more have in-principle approval and await final registration (Cafemutual).

Average assets of specialised investment funds (SIFs) rose 16.38% to ₹40,758 crore in October, net inflows fell 32.04% to ₹5,150 crore and folios rose 12.82% to 1,76,542 (Cafemutual, citing AMFI). SIFs are a separate product from mutual fund schemes.

Each scheme's category, riskometer level and terms are in its scheme information document. This list is reported for information only and is not a recommendation.

regulatory.text: From 1 April 2027, a scheme may net its payments for shares bought against receipts for shares sold in the same settlement cycle, for outright trades within each scheme only (SEBI circular).
Managers of SIFs, AIFs and portfolio management services can now certify an investor as accredited themselves, and mutual fund holdings now count towards the securities exposure test (Cafemutual).
Direct plans became the default option on fund houses' own digital platforms; investors who choose a regular plan are shown its higher expense ratio, and regular plans continue (Kotak Neo).

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation circular of 26 February 2026, an overnight fund is an open-ended debt scheme that invests in overnight securities, which mature in one day. Because each holding matures the next day, in general the interest rate and credit risk that come with longer maturities are low, though not nil. Each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: What a fixed maturity plan is
paragraphs: A fixed maturity plan (FMP) is a close-ended debt scheme: investors can put money in only during its new fund offer, and the scheme runs for a set term.
For example, an FMP with a term of about three years accepts money only during its offer period and then runs until its set maturity date.
Because the term is fixed, the scheme information document sets out its maturity date and terms, and each scheme's riskometer level is in the fund house's own documents.
